chunks.text: 5 Introduction Look up at the night sky; countless stars will delight and fa scinate you! The most beautiful object in the nighttime sky has got to be the Moon. It particularly captivated the hearts and minds of ancient Indians   who watched it travel through the glistening circle of stars every 27 days. So the Indians, like many other ancient cultures, developed 27 constellations. They conceived of these heavenly lights as repositories of the powers of the gods. Indian astrology, often called  Vedic Astrology,  has become quite popular throughout the world today. The true heart of this astrol
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: Vedic Astrology,  has become quite popular throughout the world today. The true heart of this astrology, its original core, is the 27 stars. To interpret their meaning, the most important thing to have is a deep and lucid understanding of the gods that empower them. Before diving into this exciting topic, please allow me to address a few important misconceptions about the stars The Stars are not the Signs The most prevalent and long-standing misconception about the 27 stars is that they are permanently linked with certain zodiac signs. The 12 zodiac signs are based on the movement of the Sun,
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: anently linked with certain zodiac signs. The 12 zodiac signs are based on the movement of the Sun, which we measure by observing its solstices and equinoxes. The 27 constellations are based on the movement of the Moon, which we measure by observing it moving through the stars. These different ways of measuring space don t stay aligned to one another: The solstice Sun, for example, drifts very slowly through the stars year by year. So, there is no permanent relationship between the stars and the signs.
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 7 The Stars have no  Planetary Lords  Another prevalent misconception is that the stars have  planetary lords  who play a role in forming the character of the star. This mistaken idea arises because Indian astrology associates the stars to specific planets when calculating astrological time phases (nak atra-da  ). But even then there is no permanent correlation between planets and stars because there are dozens of nak atra-da   systems, and each one associates different planets with different stars. At least for now, please forget any explanation of the 27 stars that talks about their  planeta

chunks.text: 15 The name Bhara   comes from the word b hara a, which means,  to maintain, bear, support.  The English phrase,  bearing children  or  labor pains  expresses it perfectly. The vulva is an excellent symbol for Bhara   because it symbolizes bearing children, which itself summarizes the main characteristic of this star: bringing new life into the world at the cost of great labor and pain. It seems odd that the powers of Yama, the god of death, reside in the star which bears new life. This highlights the fact that life and death are inseparable and new life is impossible without the death of the
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ts the fact that life and death are inseparable and new life is impossible without the death of the old. As expressed by  r  K   a in Bhagavad-G t  (2.27):  Death is certain for one who is born. Birth is certain for one who dies.  Life Needs Death The fundamental character of Bhara   is that good things cannot come without difficulties. Illustrating this, Mah bh rata (Vana.142) tells a story of life being unable to continue without death. The story takes place in the  First Age  of history, during which time humans have extremely long lifespans. Yama, the god of death, therefore thought it wou

chunks.text: ng which time humans have extremely long lifespans. Yama, the god of death, therefore thought it would be OK to take a break for a while. But the population of the Earth quickly became too great and she could not support everyone. Overpopulation began to cause serious problems. The gods appealed to Vi  u, who took the form of a boar to lend strength to the earth. Yama came back to his duties (making sure people die) and the situation came back to normal. In another section ( di.199), Mah bh rata tells a similar story. Yama once took the position of chief priest in a very long religious ritual,

When he did, people started dying again and everything returned to normal.

chunks.text: 16 Death may not be pleasant, but it is good and important. B hara   is like that: it contains the sacrifices that must be made to produce something worthwhile; difficulties must be endured to produce something great. Death of Death This next story illustrates a similar point. There are a few slightly different versions it, this telling is found in Padma Purana: Once upon a time, a young boy was told that he would die when he turned sixteen. Seeking protection from this fate, the boy sat in yogic meditation before a deity of  iva. When he turned sixteen, the agents of Yama tried to take him, b

Yama himself appeared personally with his noose. But when he threw the noose, the boy leapt upon and embraced his deity, crying for protection. The noose encircled both the boy and the deity, who became furious at what death appeared to be attempting. The deity sprang to life and burned the god of death to ashes. All the gods appealed to  iva to reconsider what he had just done. Without death, how would the world continue to function

chunks.text: 18 Restriction Bhara   is like the child cramped within the womb: It is a difficult star of struggles and restrictions. Indeed, the name of the god of death, Yama, literally means restriction / regulation. Death is merely the ultimate regulation, the most inescapable restriction. In Bhagavad-G t  (10.29),  r  K   a says: yama  sa yamat m aham  Among enforcers I am Yama.  Bhara   represents difficulties we must face before we can prosper. It is a star of yama: limitation and restriction. To face such trials we must develop yama: self-control. Note on Yama and Dharma The god of death (Yama) and
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: such trials we must develop yama: self-control. Note on Yama and Dharma The god of death (Yama) and the god of morality (Dharma) are different beings, frequently confused to be one. It s easy to see how this confusion would arise: Dharma (the god of morality) is also called Yama because morality requires self-control (yama). And the Yama (the god of death) is also called Dharma - because he judges people after death on the basis of their morality (dharma). Despite sharing names, however, they are different beings, and it is Yama, not Dharma, who empowers Bhara  .

chunks.text: 20 The word k  ttik  comes from the k tta / kartati, meaning  cut, divide.  Obviously the symbol of sharp blades is fitting. But the word is also related to the root k t which means  assemble, accomplish.  So the sharpness of K ttik  is not a barbarian blade! It is a careful tool of precise subdivision. Similarly, K ttik  is a star of insight, incisiveness, disassembly of complex things, and detailed comprehension. Ag i, the god of fire, empowers K ttik . Fire has two qualities: it is bright, and it is hot. Brightness illuminates. Heat burns, or  digests,  it liberates the energy within things
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: d it is hot. Brightness illuminates. Heat burns, or  digests,  it liberates the energy within things. K ttika is not only incisive but  bright.  It is a star of intellectual, brilliant insights and the ability to quickly digest concepts and ideas. The English word  critical  likely comes from k ttik . It is a star of incisive, critical thought. K ttik  is not a good star for anything requiring tenderness, but it is excellent for analysis, rapid and accurate assessment, and the ability to cut through problems and confusions. chunks.text: 25 Everything about this star symbolizes f ertile creativity.   The name Rohi   means,  red-girl.  That literally means a girl who is fertile, having entered puberty and begun her menstruation. Or you can take it as a  blushing bride.  Either way, Rohi   means  procreation , and procreation means creativity and fertility.   Rohi   s symbol, a bull, is a symbol of male fertility. The bull pulls a cart overflowing with produce; another symbol of fertility.   Rohi   s other symbol, a tree, is a symbol of fertility because trees produce fruit, which are symbolic of children. The specific tree that
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: bol of fertility because trees produce fruit, which are symbolic of children. The specific tree that symbolizes Rohi   is the Banyan, which is a particular symbol for fertility and growth because the Banyan tree never stops growing and expanding.   Rohi   s deity, Brahm , is the father of all creatures, the original progenitor, and is therefore a symbol of fertility. Brahm  is also the creator of everything in the universe, and thus a symbol of creativity. Rohi   is most certainly the star of fertility & creativity, accompanied by passion and beauty. Let s explore who Brahm  is and hear some s

Let s explore who Brahm  is and hear some stories connected with him, to better appreciate the fertile creative energy and passion within his star, Rohi  . The God of Creativity Hinduism is often portrayed to Christianized audiences as having a concept of  trinity  because Indian thought conceives of the world as being composed of three basic forces. In truth, however, the Indian concept is less like the Christian trinity and more like modern color theory, which states that three primary colors combine in various ratios to create an infi
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ern color theory, which states that three primary colors combine in various ratios to create an infinite spectrum.
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 26 The three primary forces are s attva, rajas, and tamas. Sattva = clarity, light, balance, peace Rajas = redness, passion, desire, action Tamas = shadow, darkness, stability, sleep These three forces cause three essential universal events: maintenance, creation, and destruction. Three extremely powerful beings command the three forces and therefore the three universal events. Vi  u keeps things existing by commanding the force of clarity, sattva. Brahm  creates things by commanding the reddening force, rajas.  iva destroys things by commanding the force of shadow, tamas. Brahm  is the deity
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ng force, rajas.  iva destroys things by commanding the force of shadow, tamas. Brahm  is the deity of the reddening power of creation and passion, rajas. So he is naturally the deity of the red star Rohi  . Rohi   is a star of rajas: fertility, passion, motivation, and creative powers of all sorts. Tale of Creation Vedic literature gives us a few different angles on the birth of Brahm  and how he created the world.6 I will incorporate all these as I present you the Pur  ic tale of creation: Before all else, there is consciousness. It is full of inherent joy and bliss. Joy is not stagnant. By

chunks.text: ore all else, there is consciousness. It is full of inherent joy and bliss. Joy is not stagnant. By nature it is ever-amplifying. Amplification implies an original signal and a distinct entity to amplify that signal. Plurality is therefore inherent in the original singular consciousness. Since joy does not thrive in loneliness, an infinite number of beings eternally center around the original consciousness. Those infinite beings possess freewill, and are free to be non- cooperative with this scenario. Therefore a mirror image of reality exists, 6 Manusm ti chapter one and V mana Pur  a chapter

Then you will understand.  Brahm  practiced stillness and self-control, and as a result his mind became receptive to a full transmission of knowledge from Vi  u. Before Brahm , there was nothing but what we might call subatomic quantums. Everything which now exists is a creation of Brahm  or a subsequent creation of his creation. Let s stop for a moment to consider how immensely creative Brahm  must be. He is the creator of the entire universe, the most creative being in it! chunks.text: 29 Brahm  Marries His Daughter Regarding more conventional procreation,  r mad Bh gavatam (3.12) tells a story too interesting not to mention. For Brahm  to reproduce sexually he must first create his own wife. So, in a sense, his wife must be his  daughter . Her name is V k (the power of speech, another name for S rasvat , the goddess of learning), and she was not at all into the idea. When Brahm  began pressuring her, his other children stopped him in protest. Ashamed of himself, Brahm  abandoned his body and created a new one, to wash off the impurity of his thoughts. The old body turned in
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ned his body and created a new one, to wash off the impurity of his thoughts. The old body turned into a dangerous fog in the darkness. Later on V k agreed to marry Brahm , seeing his predicament, but the two are not a happy couple and live at a distance from one another. Father of  iva  r mad Bh gavatam (3.12) describes  iva as the child of Brahm . Brahm  became furious that his quadruplet sons refused to take up the important duty of procreation, in favor of pursuing celibacy for spiritual reasons. From between his furrowed eyebrows, Brahm  s anger sprang forth personified as Rudra, who late

I will tell you this story in more detail when we come to Rudra s star,  rdr . Vi  u is the first god because he controls the power of sattva, the energy of existence itself. Existence cannot manifest itself, however, without creation   so from Vi  u comes the god of creativity (rajas),Brahm . M ga  r   s symbol   a deer sniffing the ground   is essentially a literal depiction of the word M ga  r   ( Deer s face ). Soma is the deity of M ga  r  . Soma comes up in Bhagavad-G t  (15.13), when  r  K   a says, pu   mi cau adh   sarv   somo bh tv  ras tmaka   I become Soma and make plants delicious and nourishing. chunks.text: Soma is the god of a legendary elixir (also named Soma) that grants eternal youth and unsurpassed delight. I think it is simplest to describe Soma as the  fountain of youth.  This ties in nicely with the nature of M ga  r   to inspire quests and searches. Literally, the word soma means  juice, sap, liquid.  Specifically, it is the liquid within plants that makes them nourishing and delicious. Nourishment keeps us young, deliciousness delights us; so all food is a type of Soma. The legendary elixir is simply the ultimate form of food. Vedic lore singles out one plant with the name soma-vall , f

It is now extinct, but they say that millennia ago it grew in a few specific areas,10 and its leaves blossomed and withered with the waxing and waning Moon. By pressing the juice from its stalks one could make a beverage called Soma or Am ta   the  nectar of immortality,  which the gods copiously drink to become powerful and impossible to kill. 10  g 8.7.29 & 8.64.10-11 say it grew in  Sushoma, Arjikiya, etc.  and in  Sharanyavat  (which is probab

chunks.text: 33 All v egetable-food carries the power of life in it. So in a sense, all food is am ta. If we don t eat, we die (m ta). If we eat, we don t die (a-m ta). All food makes us  immortal  because it counteracts mortality. But the elixir made from the Soma plant is a super-food of legendary power. Humans and gods alike from all ages and cultures eternally search for it, like deer sniffing out its trail. The deer of M ga  r   sniffs the ground in search of Soma in healthy and delicious herbs, but the human spirit sniffs at the paths of life in search of Soma in the form of eternality and bliss. M g

Soma, Am ta, Rasa I mentioned that foods, among which Soma is the emperor, have two qualities: they keep us alive, and give us pleasure.  g Veda (9), a section entirely dedicated to Soma, confirms this, saying that Soma (1) gives immortality, and (2)  roars . Soma is also called Am ta ( imortality ) because it counteracts mortality, food keeps us alive.  g 9.42 goes so far to calls Soma the  immortality of the immortals  and the  godhood within the gods. chunks.text: 34 Directly or indirectly, consciously or not, we are all on a q uest seeking rasa. Our ambition may be smashed into a lower, smaller shape by the hammer of repeated failure, but rasa is the real thirst behind every desire. M ga  r   involves all permutations of the search for rasa, not merely base and simple fun-seeking. After all, a deer is a beautiful and graceful creature, not a brute. Rasa is the highest objective of M ga  r  . The Upanishad tells us that we will not find rasa in its fullest form in any fruit or vegetable, nor even in any paradisiacal elixir. We find it in sah - the All-A

Siblings in the Stars Mah bh rata (Vana.221.15) tells us that Soma s brother is Ag i, and his sister is Rohi  . This is has significant astrological import. The two brothers, Soma and Ag i stand on both sides of their sister. To one side of Rohi   is Soma s star, M ga  r  . To the other side is Ag i s star, K ttik . Ag i is the solar principle, fire. Soma is the lunar principle, water. Life thrives best when heat and moisture combine. Rohi

What is a Storm? It is frightening, terrible and destructive, but it is nature s way of replenishing the clean oxygen and protective ozone in the atmosphere.  rdr  is the storm that we must weather so that our nature can once again become pure and clean.  ankara- c rya, an incarnation of Rudra, was born when the Moon was in  rdr . Clearly, this star is a spiritually fertile domain. The Creator and Destroyer Fight The Skanda Pur  a says that Brahm  once had an argument with Rudra, during which Rudra decapitated one of Brahm  s heads (originally he had five). Rudra threw the head into space, and it became the stars of M ga  r  , the nak atra which comes after Brahm  s Rohi  . In fact it is not uncommon to see the name of this star spelled   rudr .

chunks.text: 37 Anger & Destruction The birth of Rudra, god of  rdr , is described in many places with some variation.12 Here is a compilation of the tale: After Brahm  had created the major components of the universe, he needed to create living beings to populate it. First he generated four wonderful beings and said to them,  Populate the universe! , but they refused. They were completely uninterested in working within the material world, because their ambitions were purely spiritual. Brahm  became extremely angry that his first children would disobey him. Yet he also knew that their reason for rejecting
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: y angry that his first children would disobey him. Yet he also knew that their reason for rejecting his wish was valid. So he tried to control his anger, but it built up behind his eyebrows, which formed more and more drastically into a profound scowl. The power of his fury caused them to begin to glow. It became so intense that Brahm  could no longer hold it back. Instead of expressing it upon his saintly sons, he cast the anger out from his forehead and it became a dark purplish child who wailed and howled furiously.  Who am I?  it demanded to know.  You are Rudra (The Wailer, The Howler)!

Now, go to your rightful places and create offspring!  declared Brahm . chunks.text: 38 Seeing this Brahm  cried,  Dear children, please stop! D estruction must be balanced, measured and contained. It cannot proliferate without limit. Instead of creating more inauspicious beings, go now and meditate upon Godhead. This will calm you and make you auspicious.  The eleven Rudra and Rudr    consolidated themselves into a single male and female and followed Brahm  s order. By so doing Rudra and Rudr    became auspicious, and so received the names  iva ( He Who is Auspicious ), and P rvat  ( She Who has Risen Higher ). Rudra was born when Brahm  s creative ambitions were frustrated.
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

It represents all the things we must overcome before we can create and attain our desired objectives. Rudra brings destruction, which can easily become overwhelming, but which also serves a purpose.  rdr  empowers humanity to destroy, forget, and let go of inauspicious things. chunks.text: 39  rdr  allows us to unlearn, to destroy ignorance and f orget what should be forgotten. Protector of Divine Rasa Residents of the holy city of V  d vana tell a sacred legend of  iva as  Gope vara Mah deva.  This tale beautifully illustrates how destruction of the unreal and utter forgetfulness and abandonment of one s illusory ego is required before one can enter into the true beauty and pleasure of spiritual abundance. It reflects in the order of the stars. Rohi   is central, representing the blessed objective of beauty and fertility. It is nourished on both sides by the solar force of Ag i

chunks.text: blessed objective of beauty and fertility. It is nourished on both sides by the solar force of Ag i s K ttik  and the lunar force of Soma s M ga  r  . Then it is bracketed on both sides by the difficult walls of Yama s Bhara   and Rudra s  rdr . Here is a tale of how the god of  rdr  holds the key to entrance past these walls and into the blessed realm. In the middle of the full-moon-lit autumn night,  r  K   a held the mag ificent  dance of r sa,  manifesting infinite romantic beauty.  iva rushed to the spot to participate, but V  d , the goddess of V  d vana, stopped him in his tracks at th
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

She declared.  iva was crushed and dejected.  Why!?   No men enter here besides K   a,  V  d  explained.  Because you hold on to the false-identity of being a male, your presence cannot be tolerated!  From a great distance,  iva could hear and see and smell and feel the excitement of the r sa-dance. This drove him mad with desire.  I am Rudra!!!  He declared.  I can destroy everything!!! Therefore I will destroy my own male ego!

chunks.text: 40 Hearing his prayers,  r  R dh  sent her closest confidan t, Lalit , to  iva, who sat in fiery, passionate meditation at the edge of the forest. Lalit  imparted to  iva all the profound conceptions required to develop the inner ego of a purely feminine goddess fit to partake in  r  K   a s paramount revelry of r sa. Yet  iva s male body remained. Lalit  escorted him to the Yamun . By her blessing, when  iva again emerged from the water he possessed a new physical self to match his new internal self: he had the form of a divine goddess of r sa, a Gop . When  r  K   a saw this new gop  enterin

When  r  K   a saw this new gop  entering the r sa-dance hand in hand with Lalit  a surge of happiness and mischief erupted from his transcendental being. Because this gop  was none other than  iva (who is called Mahe vara, the great controller) K   a playfully nicknamed her Gope vara. chunks.text: 42 P unar means again. Vasu means bright. So the word Punarvasu can mean,  Becoming bright again  (Reignition). Punarvasu is about things happening again; Things happening within other things, within themselves; in cycles; in repetition. A fractal   an image formed by a pattern repeating itself within itself   is an excellent symbol for Punarvasu. The classical symbol is an arrow put back into a quiver after it has been shot. Mother of her own Father Here is an example of fractal patterns within patterns: The goddess of Punarvasu is Aditi   who is the mother of her own father. Aditi is the fab
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: patterns: The goddess of Punarvasu is Aditi   who is the mother of her own father. Aditi is the fabric of space itself, so she is the raw material Brahm  draws upon for creation. Thus, she is the real  mother  of Brahm  s children, including her own father Dak a. She helped create Dak a, and later she took shape in the world by being born as his daughter. The son comes from the mother, and then the mother comes from the son. Thus  g Veda (10.72.4) says:  Aditi comes from Dak a, but Dak a comes from Aditi.  Boundless Unity The name Aditi literally means boundless. She is the fabric of space it
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: from Aditi.  Boundless Unity The name Aditi literally means boundless. She is the fabric of space itself, the boundless matrix within which everything else exists. Because space is the womb within which all live develops, she is the  universal mother.  Especially the  vasu    the luminous gods   are all her children. To be boundless means to have no boundaries, to be whole, unbroken and undivided. The goddess of non-division is the mother of the gods. Her sister s name is Diti, which means divided. This goddess of division is the mother of the anti-gods. The idea emerges that unity is a godly
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ed. This goddess of division is the mother of the anti-gods. The idea emerges that unity is a godly principle, while division is ungodly. Things that unite have godly effects, while things that divide have ungodly effects.
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 43 Aditi s Punarvasu empowers humanity to work cooperatively, become unified; to come together and form a larger pattern within larger patterns. Aditi is not only the mother of the gods, but she is also the mother of the original Godhead when He appears tangibly within this universe as an avat r ( incarnation ). This is another example of fractal patterns, Aditi comes from Godhead, but Godhead comes from Aditi. Mother of God The concept of being the Mother of a being that has no origin and is the origin of everything is another perfect example of the fractal patterns- within-patterns that symb
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: e origin of everything is another perfect example of the fractal patterns- within-patterns that symbolizes Punarvasu.  r mad Bh gavatam (8.16-18) describes how Aditi became the mother of existence itself, Vi  u: A powerful demon named Bali conquered all the worlds and the gods lost all power. Aditi requested her husband Ka yapa to give her a son who could save them. Ka yapa told her how to perform a ritual for this purpose. But since Aditi knew that only Godhead could save the gods from this situation, her performance of this ritual attracted God to become her child. When the ritual was comple
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: uation, her performance of this ritual attracted God to become her child. When the ritual was complete, Godhead appeared and assured her,  I will become your son, but this situation cannot be remedied by force. I will come up with a different strategy.  Aditi then conceived a child with Ka yapa, who was born mysteriously as the Godhead Vi  u   blackish with glittering yellow clothes, four armed and gloriously beautiful. Before their very eyes, He transformed into a very small boy; a student-mendicant, named V mana. Vi  u thus became the younger brother of Aditi s first child, Indra. The young
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: icant, named V mana. Vi  u thus became the younger brother of Aditi s first child, Indra. The young boy soon set off to where Bali was performing an elaborate ritual to celebrate his victory over the gods. When he entered the arena, everyone was struck with his beauty and effulgence and greeted him
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 44 with warm respects. Bali, especially, was charmed by t he endearing beauty of V mana.  It is my great fortune that such a wondrous spiritualist has come to my palace! The opportunity to serve you will free me from all the sins of my selfish life. You must have come here to ask something from me, please ask it! I will happily give you any wealth or pleasure you desire!  V mana was very pleased with Bali s humble and spiritually informed attitude. He said to Bali,  You are wonderful because you have good teachers and because your grandfather is the great Prahl d. You are as great and dear to
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: have good teachers and because your grandfather is the great Prahl d. You are as great and dear to me as your grandfather! But I do not need any wealth or pleasures. It is not good for a spiritualist to accept such things. I just want whatever land I can claim for myself in three paces.  Bali replied,  You are wise beyond your years, but still inexperienced. You should take what you can get when it is offered! I own even the heavens. I can give you anything. Someone who asks a favor from me should never have to ask another person for a favor again! So why should you only take three paces of l

V mana replied,  If a person can t be satisfied with three steps of land, he won t be satisfied with the three worlds. Self-control makes one happy. Feeding uncontrolled desire causes misery.  Smiling, Bali said,  Alright, then. You are very wise. I shall happily give you what you request.  With that he took up his waterpot to wash his palm in a gesture of solemn promise, but no water would flow from it. When Bali used a straw to unblock the no
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

When Bali used a straw to unblock the nozzle,  ukra (the deity of Venus and Bali s guru) suddenly appeared, holding his eye in pain. He had taken a tiny form and purposely clogged the pot, and the straw had poked out his eye.  ukra said,  This little boy is Vi  u! He has been born to Aditi to protect her children, the gods. You ve gone and promised to give him land!? He will take everything from you and give it to your enemy, Indra! You fool!
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 45 You will be homeless!!! He will take the entire universe in just two steps and make you unable to fulfill your promise, and thus send you to hell! Charity is good, up to a point! Besides, you did not say  Om  when making this promise to give him land, so it is not binding!  Bali thought about this deeply for a few moments. Then he said,  Mother Earth said,  I can bear any burden, but I cannot bear a liar.  Truthfulness is the soul of morality, without which there can be no good fortune. I don t mind losing my riches, so long as I do not lose my morality.   ukra was infuriated.  You think yo

V mana then began to grow to huge proportions, revealing that he was all-pervading Vi  u. Bali could see the entire universe within his  body.  Here is another instance of fractal patterns-within-patterns: V mana was standing within the universe, yet the

With one step the huge Vi  u covered all of normal earthly space. With the second he reached the highest extent of the heavens. The anti-gods rushed forward to kill Vi  u, but Vi  u s associates appeared and drove them back effortlessly into subterranean regions. Vi  u s eagle, Garuda, then arrested Bali and tied him in ropes. V mana said to Bali,  You promised me three steps of land, but I have taken everything you possess and more, in just two steps. Sinc

Bali replied,  That is no problem. Your punishment is always just. We anti-gods always want power and prestige. When you punish us it is kind because it opens our eyes to a more blissful reality that we are not all-powerful, we are but fragments of your energy and should endeavor
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

But I do not wish to be untruthful. I have offered you three steps of property. I owned the three worlds, which you took in just two steps. chunks.text: 47  r mad Bh gavatam (10.3) says that Aditi was once P   i, th e wife of a different son of Brahm , named Sutapas. She performed great austerities in devotion to Vi  u for 12,000 years. When Vi  u appeared to grant her wishes, she wished that he would become her son, which he did. K   a told this story to his mother, to let her know that she and he are always mother and son, repeatedly. Thus K   a s mother, Devak  is yet another incarnation of Aditi. The story behind Aditi becoming Devak  is also fascinating. It is told in Dev  Bh gavata (4): Aditi was the first wife of Ka yapa, and she gave b
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: o fascinating. It is told in Dev  Bh gavata (4): Aditi was the first wife of Ka yapa, and she gave birth to the gods, headed by Indra. Her sister, Diti, the second wife, was jealous and asked Ka yapa for children who would be equals to the gods. Thus eventually she gave birth to the anti-gods ( demons ). But Aditi became fearful and sent her child to destroy the first child in her sister s womb. Diti then cursed Aditi:  Your child will repeatedly lose his kingdom to my children! And you will lose your children!  The first part of the curse is constantly being fulfilled as Diti s children, the

chunks.text: e your children!  The first part of the curse is constantly being fulfilled as Diti s children, the anti-gods, attempt to conquer the gods, and often succeed. The second part of the curse was fulfilled when Aditi became Devak , who had to suffer the loss of many children at the hands of her atrocious brother Ka sa.

chunks.text: 49 T he word pu ya has two primary meanings: 1. The top/best part of a thing; usually referring to a flower, the top and best part of a plant. 2. Nourishment; which allows us to blossom and grow. There is a motherly, loving and devotional overtone to the word pu ya. Love, after all, is the topmost blossom on the flower of life. Pu ya s primary symbol is a lotus, the most beautiful and wholesome flower. The udders of a cow are sometimes used to symbolize Pu ya; conveying the theme of nourishment. B haspati, the god of prayer and devotions, is the deity of Pu ya. In Bhagavad G t  (10.24),  r  K
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: B haspati, the god of prayer and devotions, is the deity of Pu ya. In Bhagavad G t  (10.24),  r  K   a says: purodhas   ca mukhya  m   viddhi p rtha b haspatim  Among the best priests, know me to be B haspati.  Among all priests, B haspati is the best. A priest is a person who facilitates our connection to the divine. Prayer is an interactive union with the divine. B haspati is the god who masterfully conducts religious rituals and prayers   the technologies of divine communion. Pu ya is always thought of as being among the most fortunate and prosperous of Vedic stars. Other names for Pu ya a
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: thought of as being among the most fortunate and prosperous of Vedic stars. Other names for Pu ya are Sidhya ( perfect ) and Ti ya ( auspicious ). Why? What is the connection between devotional prayer and prosperity? In G t  (10.38)  r  K   a says: n tir asmi jig  at m  For those whose desire victory, I am morality.
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 50 Pu ya is a successful and prosperous star because it f acilitated communion with the divine, which engenders morality, which leads to true victory and prosperity. What is morality? It is what distinguishes  right  from  wrong.  Right and wrong, though, are not absolute. What is right in one circumstance is wrong in another. It might be wrong to use a knife to kill someone, yet right to use the same knife for slicing bread. It might be wrong to kill someone, but right to kill someone who is on the brink of killing many other people. Morality is relative. And that s why it s complicated. We c
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: the brink of killing many other people. Morality is relative. And that s why it s complicated. We can t really be morally strong without understanding moral relativity: knowing how to apply a moral principle in many different circumstances. This requires serious contemplation, reflection, and depth. B haspati is facilitates all these things: contemplation, meditation, prayer; and by doing so he strengthens real morality, and thus causes us to be more victorious and prosperous. Through Pu ya, B haspati empowers human beings to commune with deeper principles. This strengthens morality and cause
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: haspati empowers human beings to commune with deeper principles. This strengthens morality and causes prosperity and victory. It eventually leads to selfless devotional intimacy with the divine. The Son of the Sage of Fire  g Veda (4.40.1) and Mah bh rata (Adi.66) clearly state that B haspati is the son of Angiras. Angiras is Brahm  s son, was born from the coals of a fire. He is therefore a fire-sage. His son, B haspati is sometimes called  the son of fire,  but this doesn t mean B haspati is the son of Ag i, the fire god. From his father B haspati inherits affinity and skill with fire. Fire
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: he son of Ag i, the fire god. From his father B haspati inherits affinity and skill with fire. Fire is symbolic of religion and morality because the light of fire shows us the correct path, and the warmth of fire nourishes us. Fire is the focal point of most religious rituals, especially Vedic, because it transforms things. It transforms matter to energy, thus allowing sacrifices to be delivered to the gods.
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 51 B haspati s mother is named  raddh , which means tr ust, faith, and confidence. The god of communion with the divine is born from trust, faith, and confidence. Pu ya encourages faith and devotion. Priest and Guru of the Gods B haspati was very religiously inclined from birth and therefore went to a sacred place to commune with the divine.  iva was very impressed with the boy and granted him the position of the priest and guru of all the gods, and gave him custodianship of the astrological planet Jupiter. Much of what an astrologer knows as the traits of Jupiter can therefore be transposed i
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: net Jupiter. Much of what an astrologer knows as the traits of Jupiter can therefore be transposed into Pu ya. You can think of Pu ya as if it was Jupiter as a star: It is very positive, helpful, nurturing, and allows things to grow, develop, prosper and blossom in a moral and wholesome manner. Milking the Earth  r mad Bh gavatam (4.17-18) tells a story which ties into using the udders of a cow as Pu ya s symbol: Once upon a time, the Earth became very weak and there was extreme famine. They selected B haspati to become the calf, and through him obtained  milk  from the Earth in the form of mantras and hymns that would make the mind clean and pure. B haspati entered and Indra neglected to stop his revelry to welcome his priest and guru. Seeing Indra reeking of the typical egoistic pollution that accompanies material enjoyment, B haspati simply turned around and left. chunks.text: 54 The word    le   means,  intimate connection, intimate contact, embracing, entwining, adhering, and clinging.  A coiled serpent is a fitting symbol for   le  , because serpents coil around things: embracing and entwining with them.   le   s deity is the  N ga    supernatural serpents, a.k.a.  dragons.  Like all serpents they have scales, forked tongues and powerful poisons. Unlike most serpents N ga can combust their spit poisons, usually have many heads, have super-human intellect and talent, and can shape-shift in and out of humanoid and intermediate forms. They are protectors of vast tre

chunks.text: , and can shape-shift in and out of humanoid and intermediate forms. They are protectors of vast treasures. Sometimes, ordinary snakes (particularly the King Cobra) can be called  n ga  as an honorific. All snakes are connected to   le  , but the deities of   le   are the supernatural dragons, not ordinary serpents. Rivalry and Jealousy I ll tell you a story about the origin of the N ga. One of the sons of Brahm  is Mar ci. His son is Ka yapa, the  genetic engineer of the universe.  Ka yapa married 13 sisters. With each wife he produced different species of offspring, from gods to insects. Acc

According to Mah bh rata (Adi.16), one wife, Kadru, wanted to have many, many children; while another wife, Vinata, desired only two very powerful children. Kadru laid 1000 eggs which quickly hatched into so many different varieties of serpents, the foremost of whom were the N ga. Vinata laid two eggs which took a very long time to hatch. One of the children became Aru a, who drives the chariot of the Sun and shields the world from the fury of his heat. The other was the gigantic King of Eagles, Ga

Kadru was jealous of the power her husband allotted to her sister s two children, and devised a plan to ruin her. She made a bet:  I bet you that the color of the tail of the divine horse that emerged from the ocean of milk is not white! If I am right, you and your children are my slaves. If
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

The serpents who refused their mother s request on moral grounds became a separate, special branch of the N ga race. The rest of the serpents mixed into the hair, making it appear black. Vinata thus lost the bet and became a servant of Kadru. It was then that Garu a hatched from his egg, born into slavery. He submitted but developed hatred of the serpents as a result. Eventually, he asked the N ga,  How can I be released of this d

Garu a was freed from servitude the moment he placed the nectar before the N ga. chunks.text: 57 The most celebrated tale involving V suki involves how the gods and anti-gods produced the original nectar of immortality by churning the cosmic ocean of milk. Churning a bucket of milk will make a person tired, and churning an entire ocean was a feat even for the gods to accomplish. They needed enormous apparatus like continents to stand on and mountains to churn with. The rope to turn this mountainous churning rod would have to be fantastically strong and long. Everyone agreed that the king of serpents, V suki would be the only being that could act as the rope. V suki, however, was far of

chunks.text: of serpents, V suki would be the only being that could act as the rope. V suki, however, was far off in the deepest netherworld. Garu a, proud of his ability to carry away snakes in his beak, stepped forward and announced that he would bring V suki. When he arrived and explained the situation, V suki replied,  If it s so urgent, carry me to the spot at once.  Garu a, however, could not lift V suki off the ground. Thus he returned to the gods empty handed.  iva then extended his hand to the netherworld and V suki wrapped himself around  iva s wrist like a bracelet. Thereafter, V suki firmly em

V suki cooperated happily with  iva but embarrassed haughty Garu a. It is said that snakes are enemies of common people, but they never harm a saint 13. chunks.text: 59 The divine qualities of  e a are more fully and purely realized in  e a s own star: Uttara Bh drapad . If we merely drop the  l  as an irregularity of pronunciation, the word   le   becomes  - e a -  the place of  e a.    le   interests humanity in mystical spirituality. chunks.text: 62 The word ma gha means  power  and also means  gift.  The symbol of Magh , a throne, is an image of inherited power. Indra, the king of the gods, seated on the throne of paradise is known as Maghavan. But it is the Pit  (ancestral spirits) who are the deities of Magh    signifying that we inherit power from our ancestors. Magh  bestows gifts  from our ancestors.  This literally indicates inheritance of power, career, fortune, and qualities ( DNA ). Such inheritance really comes as a result of efforts made in our previous births, so Magh  also indicates powers, qualities and abilities carried
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

Divine  Ancestors  The Manu-Sm ti s third chapter tells us that Pit  are divine beings who are the  forefathers  of us all. It says that some of Brahm  s initial mental offspring created the Pit , who in turn created powerful beings, who in turn produced the original members of the various species in the universe. chunks.text: ealm. Ancestor Worship In ancient India, the Pit  were worshipped with approximately equal importance as the gods, but the rituals were different. Rituals for worshipping the Pit  are called  r ddha and always involve grains. 15 Indeed the word magha can even connote  grain.  The  r ddha ritual highlights the mutual indebtedness between ancestor and offspring. In Vedic culture, it is the duty of every child to have at least one child of his own. This is how we repay our debt to the ancestors who paved the way for our birth, and it helps insure success of the Pit  s original duty: to populate t
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: paved the way for our birth, and it helps insure success of the Pit  s original duty: to populate the universe. The divine  ancestors  help guide us through the afterlife when we die, and when our literal ancestors die it is our duty to make an effort to help them. Therefore a child performs  r ddha on behalf of his deceased parents. The ceremony worships not the deceased but the Pit  who will make the effort to ease the passing of the deceased. 15 The  r ddha ceremony is still very popluar among Hindus, and is observed twice a year, during the waning moon of two months: A vina and Caitra. Paired nak atra share similar meanings, with subtle differences. The word ph lgun  means  reddish lady,  which should remind us of the nak atra named Rohi  , since that word has the same meaning. chunks.text: esirable (   s), which indicates that she has an appetite for romance and that she is therefore capable of fulfilling romantic desires. The name of Bhaga s wife indicates what both genders must possess if they are to truly enjoy happiness together:   Siddhi  perfection, unusual skill, and dexterity This word, siddhi, has strong spiritual implications, indicating that romantic pleasure is not an end in and of itself, but a part of what we need in our greater journey towards a more significant and spiritual understanding of love and pleasure.

chunks.text: 68 P rva Ph lgun  allows one to develop dexterity and skil l in these talents, arts, and character traits so as to enjoy a fulfilling and satisfying sensual and romantic life. Negative Effects of Lust The Mah bh rata (Sauptika Parva) tells the following story of Bhaga angering Rudra: At the end of a divine age, the gods came together to divide up the surplus shares of sacrifices they had received. The eagerness to enjoy made them feel that they could leave Rudra out of the divvy. When Rudra learned of this, he became furious and attacked. Those who were most lusty to enjoy the sacrificial port
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ned of this, he became furious and attacked. Those who were most lusty to enjoy the sacrificial portions were his main target. He cut off the hands of the god named Savit , who was lusty to feel and grab all the resources for sense gratification. He took out the teeth of the god named P   , who was lusty to enjoy fine delicacies. He plucked out the eyes of Bhaga, who was lusty to look upon attractive forms. The apologies of the gods finally placated Rudra and he was eventually pleased to return these to their owners. The story illustrates that the desire to enjoy what P rva Ph lgun  offers can
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: these to their owners. The story illustrates that the desire to enjoy what P rva Ph lgun  offers can easily bewilder us into greed and lust, the result of which is the opposite of happiness and bliss. Thus we must be on guard to maintain the primary male and female qualities of nobility (mahiman) and restraint (suvrat ). Divine Love and Romance In modern times, with the rise of extremely dualistic concepts of religion, we tend to conceive of a huge gulf between mater and spirit, god and pleasure, etc. This divisive conception was not embraced by Vedic culture. Certainly dualism has some releva

chunks.text: , etc. This divisive conception was not embraced by Vedic culture. Certainly dualism has some relevance, for not all things are identical. Selfishness and selflessness, for example, are polar opposites
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 69   and thus so are lust and love. However, the Indian conce pt of divinity neutralizes, harmonizes, and integrates all opposites. Bhaga is the god of  material  things such as romance, sex and marriage. Yet the word bhaga in the form  Bhagav n  is the most common classical Sanskrit term for a blessed being. The Pur  as even define Bhagav n as a moniker of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus, in Sanskrit culture, the division between material and spiritual transforms. Bhagav n means,  The possessor of Bhaga.  Sanskrit culture conceives of the Supreme Spirit as a being that has more Bhaga
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: possessor of Bhaga.  Sanskrit culture conceives of the Supreme Spirit as a being that has more Bhaga than anyone else: a blissful, attractive, talented and romantic entity. Par  ara Muni defines the word Bhagav n in Vi  u Pur  a (6.5.79):  To fully possess happiness (bhaga) one must have all majesty, power, fame, beauty, knowledge and detachment.  Bhaga gives majesty   which means status, influence and wealth. He gives power   which means heroism, bravery and strength. Bhaga also gives fame   which means celebrity and good reputation. He also gives beauty   which attracts others to participate
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ich means celebrity and good reputation. He also gives beauty   which attracts others to participate in ones pleasures. Money, power, fame, beauty  these first four are obvious and well known ingredients of a person who can enjoy great pleasures. Knowledge is a lesser known requirement. We need expertise and skill to really enjoy the pleasures of life. Bhaga, the god of pleasures, also gives detachment   because attachment causes suffering. If we are only attached to enjoying pleasures, we will inevitably suffer. To be detached requires knowledge of what one really is   a spiritual being, not
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: inevitably suffer. To be detached requires knowledge of what one really is   a spiritual being, not just a collection of senses to please. So in addition to giving money, power, fame, and beauty, Bhaga also gives knowledge and detachment. The complete package of six traits grants supreme pleasure.
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: 70 The personality of Godhead, especially in the intimate for m of  r  K   a, is recognized by Par  ara and his son Vy sa as the person most fit to be named Bhagav n.16 P rva Ph lgun  has the special ability to grant pleasures and wealth in a manner that befits a spiritually progressive person. It also can incline one to more deeply appreciate the spiritual pleasures and opulence of Bhagav n  r  K   a. Bhaga and Bhakti Again, to highlight how Indian theology does not stringently divide pleasure and happiness from spirituality: the Sanskrit word for romantic love and pleasure (bhaga) is made of
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: and happiness from spirituality: the Sanskrit word for romantic love and pleasure (bhaga) is made of the same root that makes the word for the yoga of divine love (bhakti). Bhakti means loving the All-Attractive Divinity in very tangible, intimate manner which includes and really culminates its brilliance in romantic forms of love. P rva Ph lgun  thus has a special fertility for producing bhaktas. For example, Arjuna, the most famous dear friend of K   a, was born on a lunar day when the Moon spanned both ph lgun  stars. 17 The primary Indian calendar ties the lunar phases and the 27 stars t o

The phase and star of the moon at the time of sunrise becomes the phase of that day, even if the actual phase itself changes before the next sunrise. Sometimes odd things happen: If the Sun rises when the moon is at the very end of Star A, the moon s normal motion can carry it through Star B and just into the very beginning of Star C by the time the next Sunrise happens. chunks.text: 73 Uttara Ph lgun  is the second in the Ph lgun  pair of stars . Most of what we discussed about P rva Ph lgun  applies to Uttara Ph lgun  as well. The difference is that while the previous Ph lgun  tends towards romance, Uttara Ph lgun  towards friendship and marriage. Uttara Ph lgun  is the star of marriage and commitments. The deity of Uttara Ph lgun  is Aryam , the brother of P rva Ph lgun  s deity, Bhaga. As you may recall from the chapter on Magh , In Bhagavad G t  (10.29),  r  K   a suggests that Aryam  is the foremost Pit : pitr    m aryam  c smi,  Among the Pit s I am Aryam .  This re
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: sts that Aryam  is the foremost Pit : pitr    m aryam  c smi,  Among the Pit s I am Aryam .  This reveals that Aryam  dwells with and functions like the Pit , well- wishing ancestors who protect us in difficult times. Aryam  is the foremost well-wisher and protector. The word aryam  literally means a dear friend. The exact, most specific meaning is, a friend who asks a girl to marry his friend. If a boy has a crush on a girl, his close friend goes to the girl and tells her about the boy in such a way as to attract her attention and affections. That friend is  aryam  . It is somewhat fitting th

Aryam  is the divine matchmaker. He pairs young men and women so that they can enjoy what Ph lgun  has to offer: love, romance and marriage. chunks.text: 76 The word h asta refers to a hand, the part of the body that grasps, moves, manipulates, and utilizes things. So the symbol of Hasta, a hand, simply illustrates its direct meaning. Hasta is the star of heightened awareness and dexterity. Savit  is Hasta s deity. He is the god of sunrise, who wakes us up and inspires us to use our hands. The word savit  means the awakener. It is made from the root  u which means  to inspire.  Savit  inspires our awakening to awareness. Savit  is connected with the Sunrise because when the Sun rises, we wake up. Light floods the world and we become aware of ou
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

Light floods the world and we become aware of our surroundings.  g Veda consistently treats Savit    the agent bestowing cognition - as the Sun, particularly the rising Sun. Eleven hymns in  g Veda are entirely in honor of Savit , and he is mentioned about 170 times throughout the book! Here are some that are relevant. 10.158.3:  Divine Savit  gives us sight as if from the mountaintop, and enables us to create.  Hasta creates  vision  (broad, far-reaching, and ambitious), and the dexterity to such visionary goals. 10.158.4:  [Savit ] puts vis

Similarly the soul spreads rays of sentience through our body and thus enables us to be conscious of our existence. Savit  is thus light and consciousness.

The first three worlds are the most important, and so are called the mah -vy h ti ( great utterance ). These are the words bh r bhuva  sva  - identifying heaven, earth, and the space in between. chunks.text: 81 The word c itr  means: excellent, brilliant, prismatic, multifarious, multifaceted, wondrous, and ingenious. Appropriately, the symbol of Citr  is an excellent gemstone, ingeniously cut into many facets to reveal its wondrous prismatic luster. The Deity of Citr  is Tva   , the god of creations which resemble that expertly cut jewel. Through Citr , Tva    empowers humanity to comprehend multi-faceted designs, and generate masterpieces and technological marvels. The Creation of Creativity Tva    is one of several Vedic deities who exist in a primordial, abstract form and later take a specific

chunks.text: is one of several Vedic deities who exist in a primordial, abstract form and later take a specific shape at some early point in universal history. For example:   Primordial Aditi, the goddess of Punarvasu, is the abstract principle of space itself, a domain in which things can exist. Later she takes a concrete form as a goddess born as a grand- daughter of Brahm .   Primodial Savit , the god of Hasta, is the abstract principle of conscious awareness. Later he takes a concrete form as a god born from Aditi.   Tva   , the deity of Citr , is similar. In primordial form Tva    is the abstract po

Later on he becomes the god of creative expertise, taking concrete form as a god born from Aditi. The abstract, primordial forms of gods exist prior to tangible creation, and thus prior to Brahm . Logically, the abstract power to create must exist before anything can be created. So the abstract form of Tva    exists before Brahm , and Brahm  must use Tva    s energy to design and create the universe in which Tva    soon takes birth as a tangible being. One, named Vi vakarm , creates for the gods. The other, named Maya, creates for the anti-gods. 20 Vi vakarm  literally means  the one who creates everything. chunks.text: 88 The main component of the word s v ti is sva, which means one s own. The meaning of the name Sv ti, therefore, has to do with becoming an individual.25 Sv ti s symbol is a new flower bud bending against the strong wind. This is a symbol of  going against the grain  and making the effort to stand out on our own as an individual. The deity of Sv ti is V yu, god of the wind that blows upon the new bud, making it strong. We will discover that V yu is the god of Pr  a, which creates individuality in material beings. He once held a contest of strength with the N ga king, V suki. V yu couldn t remove V suki from his grip on a mountain, but neither could V suki escape from V yu s grip. Vi  u finally called a halt to the exhausting stalemate. When V suki unwound from the mountain V yu ripped the peak from its roots and threw it far to the south. It landed in the ocean and became the isle of Lanka. V yu is also the father of the mighty warriors Hanuman and Bh ma. The Breath o

chunks.text: 89 B hadaranyaka Upanishad illustrates that nothing is more ess ential to life than V yu / oxygen: The gods of the human body held a contest to see who among them was the most important. Selecting a man to serve as the arena for their contest, one by one the different deities left that man s body. When the god of vision left, the man became blind and morose. Similarly when other deities abandoned him the man lost important functions. But when V yu stood up to leave the man, every deity of the body became uprooted and forced to leave, too. V yu sat back down and everyone returned to normal. Eve

Everyone admitted that nothing is more important to an individual s existence than V yu: god of breath. Our existence as an individual rests upon V yu s power:  life air  (pr  a or, perhaps, oxygen in modern terms). Here are several quotes illustrating this. Katha Upanishad (1.3.1) says:  The individual soul floats on the life-air in the core of the individual.   r mad Bh gavatam (4.29.71) says:  Without life-air we lose our sense of  I. Mundaka Upanishad 3.1.9 says:  The wise perceive the individual soul floating on five life-airs. The true individual does not manifest until it is purified of contact with those airs.  Indian thought holds the life-air to be a bridge element between matter and spirit. chunks.text: 93 The root of the word Vi  kh  is    kha, which means branch, division, or fork. The prefix vi indicates something that is: apart from, distinct, intense, and opposite. A branch or fork represents a decision. So   kha means a decision. Adding the prefix vi- indicates being intensely and distinctly decisive, not at all straying here and there on many different forks in the road. I translate vi  kh  as  One-pointed.  Sanskrit Lexicographers state that vi  kh  is a term for an archer s ideal attitude in shooting a bow. He selects a target, aims carefully, and does not waver in the least. The mos
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ude in shooting a bow. He selects a target, aims carefully, and does not waver in the least. The most famous archer of Indian lore is Arjuna. It is said that when he would aim his arrow he would not even see anything except the exact spot at which he was aiming. This nicely illustrates the decisive focus Vi  kh  can impart to us. The symbol of Vi  kh  is a finish line, a target, a goal. I think the appropriateness is obvious. Vi  kh  grants the ability to stay on course and make it as straight as possible to the finish line, the goal of the journey. There is a famous verse in Bhagavad-Gita (2.

chunks.text: 94 The Power to Get Things Done Vi  kh  s deity is Indr g i. Some people suggest that Indr g i refers to two different gods: Indra and Ag i taken together. However, Mah bh rata and  g Veda treat Indr g i as a single deity. For example,  g Veda (3.12) is a prayer to Indr g i. Mah bh rata (Sabha.11) mentions Indr g i in the course of describing all the supernatural beings that attend Brahm . Two forms of fire attend the Creator: Ag isoma and Indr g i. These are the two forms of fire required for religious rituals. Ag isoma is at Brahm  s service so that the Creator can have health and vitality (
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

Indr g i is at Brahm  s service so that he can obtain divine intelligence and power by worshipping Vi  u. 27 As you can see, there are many different types of fire (ag i). The foremost (indra) is the fire used in sacrifices and rituals. Thus, Indr g i is the god of ritual fire. We must put ourselves in a Vedic mindset before we can really understand what the god of ritual fire has to do with Vi  kh , the star of singular and decisive dedic
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

Vi  kh  is all about decisive commitment to an objective, and Indr g i is the god that enables us to achieve that objective. The prefix anu- means  after, under, near, following, next, and towards.  If Vi  kh  is originally  R dh   then the literal meaning of the name for the next star is obvious: Anu-R dh ,  The star that follows R dh .  Vi  kh  is the star of singular dedication and Anur dh  is very similar,

This indicates that Vedic people strove to live by the principles of love, and they made their laws on that basis, considering love to be the essence of all rules and laws. Love has two polarities: love (selfless) and lust (selfish). In Sanskrit, prema is selfless love, and k ma is selfish love, lust. Mitra is love - meant to bring joy to others and bind us to others. chunks.text: 103 The word j ye  h  means,  chief, best, greatest, first, eldest.  Indra is the deity of Jye  h , and the words indra and jye  h  are synonyms. Both mean  eldest  in the sense of being first and foremost. Indra is  Jye  h   - He is the firstborn of the gods. The title  Indra  is also given to the Supreme Godhead Vi  u, for it generically means  the best, the first, the eldest.  Generally, however, as a proper noun it refers to a god who is the king of paradise. Vedic literature has three main branches, each of which encapsulates a specific aspect of Indian culture. The Veda themselves repres
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: branches, each of which encapsulates a specific aspect of Indian culture. The Veda themselves represent ritualistic, materialistic culture. The Upanishads represent scientific and philosophical culture. The Puranas represent devotional culture. Indra is of prime importance   the God of Gods   in the Vedas, but his position is diminished significantly in the Upanishads and Puranas. This is because of what Indra inherently is. He is the king of paradise, the ultimate trademark of a living being enjoying life to its fullest extent. Thus his divinity is of unsurpassed significance for the ritualis
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: joying life to its fullest extent. Thus his divinity is of unsurpassed significance for the ritualistic materialism dominating the Veda. But in the philosophical Upanishads and devotional Puranas his light is dimmed tremendously. The  g Veda presents Indra as being very handsome and of golden complexion. In his hand is a weapon of thunderbolts, made by the divine architect Tva   . The wind himself, V yu, drives Indra s brilliant golden chariot through the heavens (thus Indra is one of the 8 original solar-deities,  dityas, of  g Veda). He constantly drinks Soma and is therefore exceedingly pow
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: inal solar-deities,  dityas, of  g Veda). He constantly drinks Soma and is therefore exceedingly powerful and delighted. The Pur  as, however, focus far more on his flaws. This is because the Pur  as downplay what Indra intrinsically represents: the height of self- oriented enjoyment and prosperity. So throughout the Pur  a we find tale after tale of Indra getting into trouble and making proud mistakes. A particularly poignant story in this regard is told in Padma Pur  a 1.56:

chunks.text: 104 Indra fell in love with the beautiful wife of a powerful yogi (Gautama). He assumed the form of her husband and came to her saying,  Lust has taken hold of me, let s make love!  The yogi knew what was happening so he rushed back to his hermitage. When he saw Indra enjoying his wife, he cursed the god,  You seem to be so dedicated to vagina that you will do anything, no matter how wrong, to enjoy one; here then, let one thousand vaginas cover your body, and let your balls fall off! In an act of defiance and insult he stole Indra s royal umbrella and the earrings of his mother, Aditi. Indra sought the help of  r  K   a, who along with his courageous wife Satyabh m  mounted the great eagle, Garu a, and flew directly into battle. They destroyed Naraka and returned the stolen umbrella and earrings to Indra. Indra invited them to enjoy his hospitality in paradise. While there, Aditi taught many paradisic arts to Satyabh m . While leaving she requested from K   a a flower from Indra s most

When K   a took this flower without asking, Indra became insulted and had to be defeated in a battle with K   a, who took the entire tree in the end! Jye  h  empowers humans to become like Indra: to be best, first, foremost, and kingly. It also has flaws similar to the flaws Indra possesses: to be intoxicated by power. One day when he was six or seven years old, he saw his father and the men of the village busy doing something apparently very important.  Dad, what is going on?  He asked.  Don t worry, go play with your friends!   You have to educate me!  K   a replied. His father smiled, full of affection. Other s came over to enjoy the conversation. chunks.text: 107  For who?  K   a asked.   For Indra.   Why?  K   a asked.  Because we are farmers and Indra is the god who controls the rain.   Dad, have you ever seen Indra?  K   a asked? His father was at a loss for words, so K   a continued,  You say Indra is responsible for our well-being, but we don t even see him. And what s more we see rain falling on the ocean where no one ever worships Indra.  The men were dumbfounded to hear a young child speak like this.  I see cows!  K   a said.  I see rivers. chunks.text: 110 The Sanskrit word m  la means,  Root, bottom, foundation, origin, beginning, and primary.  It even refers to a  corpse,  perhaps because the body is the root of ego and of our connection to a world that in always in a state of destruction. Its connection to  roots  is a symbol that reveals M la s proclivity towards herbalism, medicines and drugs. It also expresses M la s penchant for seeking the origin, beginning, and unseen root of things. M la belongs to the goddess Nir ti, the goddess of destruction. The word nir ti has two parts nir- and  ta.  ta means,  true, luminous, proper, right,
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: destruction. The word nir ti has two parts nir- and  ta.  ta means,  true, luminous, proper, right, lawful.  The prefix, nir-, means,  without.  So, Nir ti means  unlawful, improper, dark, false, and evil.  M la impels humanity towards lawlessness and an untamed spirit. Mah bh rata (Adi.66.54) depicts Nir ti as the wife of Adharma (Immorality). They have three sons, Bhaya (Fear), Mah -Bhaya (Terror), and Antaka (Murder). Ag i Pur  a (chapter 51) says that Nir ti should be worshipped wielding a sword and riding on a donkey. Dev  Bh gavata (8th division) says that she dwells in a city called  In
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: word and riding on a donkey. Dev  Bh gavata (8th division) says that she dwells in a city called  Ink Black  ( K     jana ), and is the guardian of the South-East, a direction symbolic of pain and suffering. Nir ti the Destroyer has both a male and female form, a  Rudra  and  Rudr   .  The chapter on Rudra s star,  rdr , has much to say which is pertinent to  rdr  s sister-star, M la. In particular it s important to recall that the Howling Destroyer (Rudra) becomes the Auspicious One ( iva) after directing his attention to spiritual pursuits. M la provides impetuses and resources that are very
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: r directing his attention to spiritual pursuits. M la provides impetuses and resources that are very well suited for spiritual paths. It therefore inspires humanity towards spiritual pursuit: seeking the root of all things, destroying illusions, and going beyond the limitations of what is superficial.

chunks.text: 111 Transforming Destruction into Auspiciousness Atharva Veda (5.7) depicts Nir ti in two forms: one is horrific and ghoulish, while the other is blonde, fair, golden-clad and wealthy: Misfortune, go far away! We deflect your arrow! We know you well, Nir ti! Oppressor, destroyer! A wild, naked woman haunting our dreams, Confusing and baffling us I respect you, blonde Nir ti Vast as all of space Full of auspiciousness, golden-complexioned, reclining on gold, dressed in gold, I respect you. The first form of Nir ti is unfortunate, baffling and confusing. It is an oppressive, destructive, naked u
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: rst form of Nir ti is unfortunate, baffling and confusing. It is an oppressive, destructive, naked undead who haunts our thoughts. The second is auspicious, golden, blonde and spread throughout space. M la is fearsome and destroys us. But when we respect the function of destruction as a necessary stage prior to a new creation, we receive auspicious and beneficial energy from M la. When destruction takes place things are flattened and laid low, razed to the ground, only the roots remain. Corpses or their ashes are put underground, or into water so that they soak into the earth. Destruction (Nir
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: or their ashes are put underground, or into water so that they soak into the earth. Destruction (Nir ti) is intimately tied to what is low and deep (M la). The goddess of destruction works through M la. Few people seek destruction, but it is nonetheless an essential part of the balance of nature. It would be good to review the chapters on Bhara   (star of the god of death) and  rdr  (star of the god of destruction and storms) to remember how negative things are essential to positive things.

Elephant tusks are certainly invincible. They smash through anything that stands in their way, but P rva A   h  is not like a bulldozer. chunks.text: 119 Uttara A   h  is the second in the A   h  pair; the second  elephant tusk.  As with all the paired stars, the second shares all the main themes of the first, with some subtle yet important differences. Uttara A   h  is like P rva A   h  in granting power to humanity, but it differs from the former by being less self-oriented and more inclined to consolidate power and resources from many diverse supporters. This is because the deity of Uttara A   h  is not a singular being but a complete plurality of all the gods and goddesses. The invincibility of this second A   h  comes from the ability
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: ality of all the gods and goddesses. The invincibility of this second A   h  comes from the ability to pull together many divergent resources and make them work for a common purpose. Both A   h  stars are invincible and undefeatable   but Uttara A   h  lacks the soft, watery element which made P rva A   h  s power more appealing. Thus Uttara A   h  appears more literally undefeatable and unchallengeable, much like an elephant storming through a gate. All Inclusive Divinity Vi va literally means,  all, every.  Deva means  divinity.  The fundamental meaning of the word Vi vadeva is,  every divin
chunks.source: 27 Stars, 27 Gods The Astrological Mythology of Ancient India (Vic DiCara, Vraja

chunks.text: all, every.  Deva means  divinity.  The fundamental meaning of the word Vi vadeva is,  every divinity.  The  g Veda adopts this meaning and has many prayers directed to all the gods, on the principle that no divinity should be left out from praise. As Vi vadeva, all the gods cooperate together under a central deity, usually Indra (see  g 3.54.17). Vi  u Pur  a and other Pur  as do not ignore this meaning, but give an additional definition of the Vi vadeva as one of nine special groupings of divinity. There are usually 10, sometimes 12, deities counted in this group, all of whom are said to b

chunks.text: vinity. There are usually 10, sometimes 12, deities counted in this group, all of whom are said to be children of Vi v , one of the daughters of the universe s genetic engineer, Dak a. These deities control the various powers required to be a well-rounded and successful individual. From either angle, the Vi vadeva empower humanity to draw upon a large pool of resources, and become successful as a

chunks.text: 9 CHAPTER I: VEDIC ASTROLOGY, A PERSPECTIVE An astrologer hailing from India, on arriving in North America, comes across several new names for the system of astrology that he was trained in. Hindu astrology, vedic astrology, Jyotish, etc. Of these, hindu astrology is in a sense a misnomer. Hinduism is a religion and although it has influenced Indian astrology, particularly by adding the emphasis on reincarnation, past-life experiences and the karma/dharma angle, the two perhaps should be dealt separately. The term vedic astrology refers to its origin in the Vedas -- four epic tomes allegedly r

chunks.text: eparately. The term vedic astrology refers to its origin in the Vedas -- four epic tomes allegedly recorded centuries ago and perhaps centuries apart from one another that embody the verbal and other records of the ancient cultures of India -- and other ancillary texts also allude to astronomical and astrological principles. Jyotish or Jyotir-vidya (Jyoti = light, vidya = knowledge or study) literally means the study of light, or of the illuminated (heavenly) bodies and therefore includes astronomy and astrology. The main-stream Jyotish practiced today has incorporated the Arabian/Persian Taji

The main-stream Jyotish practiced today has incorporated the Arabian/Persian Tajik system very nicely and hence modern Jyotish may now be called truly transcultural without raising any eyebrows or turning up of noses! Another thing our astrologer from India faces on crossing the oceans is the mysterious veil that still surrounds the topic of Indian astrology in the west, enhanced by the disjointed bits and pieces of information available regarding its mode of operation. India for the past many centuries had been invaded by foreign cultures and it is not unreasonable to speculate that some deliberate attempts could have been made by the bearers of 'knowledge' to codify and to make the documented and memorized knowledge in their possession as i

However, a majority of texts when talking about yogas or combination in a given house do not specify either method, leaving it to the reader/interpreter to decide which one to choose. Some, in fact, recommend using the whole sign regardless of the rising degree. According to t

According to this method of slicing the celestial zodiacal pie into 12 segments, regardless of whether the first or the last degree of a sign is rising, any planet anywhere in that sign would be considered as occupying the first house. It is understandable that this would make us computer-toting modern astrologers rather uneasy, but let us put our electronic abacii away and think for a moment. Is it not true that house divisions are really attempts to impose on the chart a mathematically- precise and ordered
