In Hindu mythology the Nakshatras, were discovered by Daksha, and are personi ed as daughters of this procreator (Prajapati Daksha) and as the mythological wives of Chandra, the Moon god. Some puranas also refer to the nakshatras as the daughters of Sage Kashyapa another Manas Putra (Mind born son of Lord Brahma) and the brother of Daksha Prajapati. A nakshatra or lunar mansion is

A nakshatra or lunar mansion is one of the 27 or 28 divisions of the sky, identi ed by the prominent star(s) in them, that the Moon passes through during its monthly cycle, as used in Hindu astronomy and astrology. Therefore, each represents a division of the ecliptic similar to the zodiac (13 20  each instead of the 30  for each zodiac sign). The orbit of the moon is 27.3 days, so the Moon takes approximately one day to pass through each nakshatra. Dr. David Frawley in his Introduction to Nakshatras says  It was to the Moon t

chunks.text: rough each nakshatra. Dr. David Frawley in his Introduction to Nakshatras says  It was to the Moon that the ancient people  rst looked for calculating time and connecting to the stars. The Moon is the basis of the heavenly clock. The  rst zodiac, therefore, would have been lunar.  He further says:  the Vedic Nakshatras arose from such a spiritual perception of the cosmos. The Nakshatras represent the abodes into which the fruits of our labour, our karma, is transferred and stored. The Nakshatras are the mansions of the Gods or  8

The 27 nakshatras o er a deeper analysis of personality, character and temperament in comparison to the twelve zodiac signs. They re ect the most intimate aspects of one s mental, emotional, physical, astral and spiritual nature. The nakshatras are an important tool for self-discovery and is an instrument to help us study and provide deeper insights. In Indian astrology the Moon Nakshatra is the main indicator of personality types,

chunks.text: deeper insights. In Indian astrology the Moon Nakshatra is the main indicator of personality types, much like the Sun sign is in Eastern astrology. The Moon s Nakshatra and its qualities is an important tool of self-discovery and useful for all counselling and psychological purposes, giving an insightful new way to look at the world. The Nakshatras are also the basis of the mantras or primal sounds of he soul used for naming children in India and for yogic practices as well. Each of the nakshatras is governed as 'lord' by one of the nine graha in the following sequence: Ketu (South Lunar Node

This cycle repeats itself three times to cover all 27 nakshatras. The lord of each nakshatra determines the planetary period known as the dasha, which is considered of major importance in forecasting the life path of the individual. In general, many scholars have used the starting point for the nakshatras as the point on the ecliptic directly opposite to the star Spica or Chitra Nakshatra. It is called Meshadi or the "start of Aries". The ecliptic is divided into each of the nakshatras eastwards starting from this point. Each planet radiates certain vibratory frequencies. They can be called as the energy distribution centres or the focal points of energy channels (vibration frequencies). The planets make their impact on the zodiacal  eld and draw their  avour from these cosm

Historical and Contemporary Use of Nakshatras Primarily nakshatras were used to determine the timing for conducting a religious  re ritual. The position of the Moon was also critical to the successful outcome of any ritual or sacri ce. In addition to their traditional usage, contemporary usages of the nakshatras include: The nakshatras are classically been used in electional astrology or for muhurta based predictions. The Equal and Unequal Division Scheme of Nakshatras We get the description of unequal nakshatra division in the works of Bhaskaracharya (an Indian mathematician and astronomer from the 7th century,and considered the most important scholar of Aryabhata's astronomical school), where he states that it was introduced by the early sages such as Garga Rishi. There is very little information in the Samhitas, Brahmanas, Upanishads, Tantras, Itihasas and the Puranas (or shall we say many of this has been lost in time) related to this unequal nakshatra division system. In this unequal nakshatra division system there are 15 nakshatras of normal length which is 13  10' 35   which is the mean daily motion of the Moon. The nakshatras Bharani, Ardra, Ashlesha, Svati, Jyeshtha and Satabhisaj were of half the above length and the nakshatras Rohini, Punarvasu, Uttara Phalguni, Vishakha, Uttara As
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: of half the above length and the nakshatras Rohini, Punarvasu, Uttara Phalguni, Vishakha, Uttara Ashada and Uttara Bhadrapada were of one and half times the normal length, and Abhijit Nakshatras length was only 4  14' 15   the residue fo the circle. The sidereal orbital period of the Moon takes around 27.323 days. A sidereal day is 23 hours 56 minutes and 4.1 seconds. The balance of 0.323 days which equates to 7 hours 44 minutes of the sidereal day was considered to be associated with Abhijit Nakshatra which equals to the zodiacal span of 4  14' 15 . The stellar sidereal zodiac of Abhijit cor
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: akshatra which equals to the zodiacal span of 4  14' 15 . The stellar sidereal zodiac of Abhijit corresponds to 6 40  - 10  53' 20   Capricorn or extends from the last pada (quarter) of Uttara Ashadha Nakshatra and it extends up to 1/15th part of Shravana Nakshatra in the equal 27 nakshatra system. Abhijit is associated with the star Vega (Alpha Lyrae). This is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra. To accommodate a uniform system of stars an equal division system was accepted by scholars of vedic astrology in the later years and accepted the theory of Chitrapaksha in which the star Chi
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: of vedic astrology in the later years and accepted the theory of Chitrapaksha in which the star Chitra or Alpha Virginis (a  xed star which corresponds to around 30  Virgo in the sidereal zodiac) was taken to occupy the middle point of the Nakshatra Mandala which is the same as the middle point of Chitra Nakshatra. This was later superimposed on the Bhagola Chakra (The ecliptic zodiacal circle) of middle point between sidereal Virgo and Libra. As regards to the unequal nakshatra division system which includes the 28 Nakshatras scheme, it is very di cult to say with certainty whether the divis
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: which includes the 28 Nakshatras scheme, it is very di cult to say with certainty whether the division started from Ashwini or any other nakshatras like Krittika, Ardra, Magha, Chitra, Shravana or Dhanistha. There are various mythological legends which give reference to these stars at some stages where considered as the middle point of the Nakshatra Mandala.  11
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: In recent history, the more accepted system for many astrologers in India has been Chitra Paksha and Revati Paksha with Lahiri's Ephemeris. This is a very debatable and also a topic of research interest to many scholars who have tested and researched with tropical ephemeris and various other middle point nakshatras schemes based on modern understanding and interpretations of the ancient astronomical works (Siddhantas) of the Indians. In this book, we have considered the initial point of the equal division system starting from Ashwini as it more prevalent in use now and the middle point of 27 n
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: l division system starting from Ashwini as it more prevalent in use now and the middle point of 27 nakshatra scheme as Chitra Paksha (Spica). Nakshatra Padas In Jyotisha shastra, the nakshatra based system is the one that corresponds/aligns the moon and constellations (Lunar Zodiac or Lunar Mansions). The Moon takes about 27.3 days to complete its sojourn around the ecliptic. The nakshatras represent the average daily movement of the Moon against the  xed stars. Each daily segment is identi ed by a small constellation or a single star. Originally the length of each nakshatra varied, but by the
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: y a small constellation or a single star. Originally the length of each nakshatra varied, but by the time the Surya Siddhanta was written (c. 500 CE), a classical astronomy text, the segments were  xed to a length of 13 degrees 20 minutes of arc. Multiplying this length by 27 equals the entire zodiacal belt of 360 degrees. Each Nakshatra is divided into 4 equal parts of 3 degrees 20 minutes each. They are called Nakshatra Pada 1, 2, 3, and 4. Therefore, in 3 Nakshatras we have 12 padas. Because each pada represents a sign of the Zodiac, in a group of 3 Nakshatras we  nd the entire zodiac in th
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: each pada represents a sign of the Zodiac, in a group of 3 Nakshatras we  nd the entire zodiac in the form of pada signs. Every human being pursues one or more of four main aims/purpose of life: Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha. Body, Mind, Spirit and Prana (Life Force). East, South, West, North. The 27 Nakshatras are studded with one or more of these. Each Nakshatra represents certain gunas. There are three levels. Scriptures such as Taittiriya Brahmana. Narad Puran and Agni Puran have also de ned the importance of Nakshatras in great detail.  12
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Nakshatra Attributes/Classi cations Deity The myths surrounding the Deities have a lot to reveal about the Nakshatras themselves. For instance there is a myth that Lord Narayana taught astrology to the Ashwini Kumaras, hence Ashwini Nakshatra supposedly indicates astrology. The Deities can also be worshipped to increase the growth of those attributes falling in their corresponding Nakshatra.  21
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Symbol Symbols are key to understanding Nakshatras. They reveal the hidden meaning of Nakshatras. Our ancient seers used symbols because they did not want such powerful knowledge to be misused. It is important to meditate on these symbols to unlock it s true potential. Shakti Each Nakshatra has its own Shakti, which means power. The Shakti of the Nakshatras is the Shakti of the deity ruling the Nakshatra. Basis Above The foundation of the power of the consciousness.  23
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Basis Below The natural reciprocation, or re ection, of the Basis Above. Result of the Shakti and Basis Above/Basis Below The natural result of the Shakti's and Basis, once applied with  exibility and imagination will yield very revealing results.  24
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Guna Guna indicates the activating motivation of the Nakshatras. Sattva - Motivation for harmony, elevation, purity. Represents the sustenance force in the universe. Rajas - Motivation for ful lling actions or desires. Represents the creative power in the universe. Tamas - Motivation for inaction. Represents the destructive force, which is required for a new beginning.  28
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Nakshatra Disposition The disposition inclines the Nakshatras to be better suited for di erent tasks. For instance moveable Nakshatras will give greater growth to those things that require movement, travel, or change. Fierce/severe Nakshatras will give greater growth to those things requiring force, such as  ghting, etc. Dhruva or Sthira Nakshatras (Fixed or Permanent) - They are  rm in their belief system. They do not move a lot. Once they make a decision, it is tough for them to change and adapt. Chara Nakshatras (moveable or ephemeral) - They interact with the world by constantly moving, ch
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: pt. Chara Nakshatras (moveable or ephemeral) - They interact with the world by constantly moving, changing, and blending into whatever environment they temporarily inhabit. Chara Nakshatras evolve quickly and frequently recreate their forms for circumstantial adaptability. In a  ght, they will probably choose to  ee. Tikshna (sharp, hard or dreadful, brutal, violent and ruthless) - They are domineering in their respective environments and very forceful in their approach to life. They can be quite impartial lacking empathy. Ugra (aggressive, passionate, driven, protective and living life to the
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: e impartial lacking empathy. Ugra (aggressive, passionate, driven, protective and living life to the fullest) - They interact with the world in a pro-active manner and constantly modify their surroundings. They often tend to be forceful, like the Tikshnas, but their approach is much warmer and emotionally charged. Laghu & Kshpira (light & swift, mentally acute, cunning & witty) - They have an innate advantage in business and health. Laghu Nakshatras tend to outsmart their opponents when con ict arises in life, making their position highly auspicious. Mridu (soft and tender, highly sensitive) -
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: arises in life, making their position highly auspicious. Mridu (soft and tender, highly sensitive) - They are artistic, empathetic, intuitive and emotional. Relationships between friends and lovers are given a lot more importance. Mridu nakshatra natives tend to value sharing and communion above everything else. Misra (a mix of soft & sharp) - A combination of Mridu's sensitivity and Tikshna's ability to destroy unwanted in uences. There are only two Misra nakshatras, Krittika and Vishahka, and interestingly both are under the in uence of the Fire God Agni. Misra's soft/sharp nature embodies t
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: interestingly both are under the in uence of the Fire God Agni. Misra's soft/sharp nature embodies the ability of  re to either warm, burn, sustain or decay.  29
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Gana (Race) / Nakshatra Temperament Each nakshatra is classi ed as Deva, Manushya and Rakshasa. Deva Nakshatra are inclined to uphold what they believe is good. Manushya Nakshatra are pragmatic and versatile in nature, they do what they believe will give the most optimum results. Rakshasa Nakshatra are inclined to break taboos, protocols, restrictions, etc. Deva (Godly) nakshatras are Ashwini, Mrigashirsha, Punarvasu, Pushya, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, and Revati. Manushya (Human)nakshatras are Bharani, Rohini, Ardra, Shravana and all the Purva and Uttara Nakshatras. Rakshasa (Demon) nakshatras a
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: rani, Rohini, Ardra, Shravana and all the Purva and Uttara Nakshatras. Rakshasa (Demon) nakshatras are Krittika, Ashlesha, Magha, Chitra, Vishakha, Jyestha, Mula, Dhanistha, and Shatabhishak.  31
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Tri Murti Association Each Nakshatra is associated with one of the Tri Murtis - Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva. Creation or Brahma Nakshatra indicates the creative aspect. Additionally these are also Karma (action) Nakshatras. Preservation or Vishnu Nakshatras are the re ection of the Brahma Nakshatra and thereby preserve or maintain what is created. These are also Bhoga (enjoyment) Nakshatras. Dissolution or Nasha (destruction) or Shiv Nakshatra indicates that which happens between the creative aspect and its re ection. Namely the process of understanding that results in the loss of the many in view o
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: nd its re ection. Namely the process of understanding that results in the loss of the many in view of the One. These are also Nasha (loss) Nakshatra.  32
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Activity Each Nakshatra is classi ed based on the activity. They are Active, Passive and Balanced. Passive Nakshatras are more receptive. Active Nakshatras are more initiative. Balanced Nakshatras are both active and passive depending upon the situation. # Nakshatra Activity 1 Ashwini Passive 2 Bharani Balanced 3 Krittika Active 4 Rohini Balanced 5 Mrigashira Passive 6 Ardra Balanced 7 Punarvasu Passive 8 Pushya Passive 9 Ashlesha Active 10 Magha Active 11 P . Phalguni Balanced 12 U. Phalguni Balanced 13 Hasta Passive 14 Chitra Active 15 Swati Passive 16 Vishakha Active 17 Anuradha Passive  33
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Purusharatha/Motivation Nakshatra Purusharthas indicates the goal or purpose of the Nakshatra. Dharma - To  nd the purpose of life Artha - Material well-being. Kama - Balanced ful llment of your desires. Moksha - Freedom from worldly su ering. The bene c or male c in uences upon the planet falling in a Nakshatra will determine to what extent the goal will be realized  35
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Body Parts Each Nakshatra is associated with a body part and this is primarily useful for medical astrology.  36
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Tridosha Nakshatras are further classi ed based on their Dosha. Ayurveda is based on the three constitutions, the three doshas. The three doshas are Vata, Pitta and Kapha. Vata (Adhya) - Literally translated, Vata means wind. Vata consists of space and air that are symbolic of in nite possibility, movement and change. Characteristic of high energy, intelligent people with creative minds, the Vata Dosha promotes mental ability and harmony. When Vata is balanced you feel, lively, enthusiastic and open-minded. When out of balance you may experience anxiety, insomnia, dry skin, weight gain. You wi
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: open-minded. When out of balance you may experience anxiety, insomnia, dry skin, weight gain. You will become rigid in your way of thinking and have di culty focusing. Pitta (Madhya) - The Pitta dosha controls digestion, metabolism, and energy production. This is a good time to have a meal. The primary function of Pitta is transformation. When pitta is predominant, a  ery nature manifests in both body and mind. Kapha (Antya) - Kapha is what makes things stick together, when kapha is dominating you feel con dent and ful lled. When functioning well, Kapha is a kind, supportive and reliable perso
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: ou feel con dent and ful lled. When functioning well, Kapha is a kind, supportive and reliable person; when out of balance they may lack motivation, gain weight and su er from allergies.  38
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Varna (Caste) There are four Varnas (caste) under which the 27 nakshatras are classi ed. It is not just a worldly classi cation but there is a deeper spiritual meaning. 1. Brahmin (Priests) - The source of Spirituality. 2. Kshattriya (Warriors) - Responsibility to protect the world. 3. Vaishya (Merchant) - Responsibility to sustain and nurture through trade/ business 4. Shudra (Service) - Responsibility to be of service.  39
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Gotra (Clan) The Saptarishis (7 Sages) were recognized as the 'mind-born sons' (Sanskrit:          , manasa putra) of Brahma, the representation of the Supreme Being as Creator. They are considered to be the ancestors of the Gotras of Brahmins. In some parts of India, people believe these are seven stars of the Big Dipper named "Vasistha", "Marichi", "Pulastya", "Pulaha", "Atri", "Angiras" and "Kratu". The Saptarishis   Marichi (name translates as the  Light and the Swift One )   Vashistha (name translates as the  Possessor of Wealth )   Angiras (name translates as the  Fiery One )   Atri (nam
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: translates as the  Possessor of Wealth )   Angiras (name translates as the  Fiery One )   Atri (name translates as the  One who Consumes  or  One who Devours )   Pulastya (name translates as  One having Smooth Hair )   Pulaha (name translates as the  Bridger of Space )   Kratu (name translates as the "One who Inspires )  40
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Important Observations Marichi Gotra: Ashwini, Pushya and Abhijit are also Laghu and Kshipra Nakshatras, with the exception of Hasta Vashistha Gotra: Bharani (Ugra), Ashlesha (Tikshna), Vishakha (Misra), Shravana (Chara) hence dual natured Angiras Gotra: Krittika (Misra), Magha (Ugra), Anuradha (Mridu), Dhanishtha (Chara) hence dual natured Atri Gotra: Rohini (Sthira), Purva Phalguni (Ugra), Jyeshtha (Tikshna), Shatabhisha (Chara) two (re)productive and two destructive Pulastya Gotra: Mrigashira (Mridu), Uttara Phalguni (Sthira), Mula (Tikshna), Purva Bhadrapada (Ugra) hence dual natured Pulah
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: (Mridu), Uttara Phalguni (Sthira), Mula (Tikshna), Purva Bhadrapada (Ugra) hence dual natured Pulaha Gotra: Ardra (Tikshna), Hasta (Laghu & Kshipra), Purva Ashada (Ugra), Uttara Bhadrapada (Sthira) hence dual natured Kratu Gotra: Punarvasu (Chara), Chitra (Mridu), Uttara Ashada (Sthira), Revati (Mridu) hence Soft, Movable and Fixed.  41
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Pancha Mahabhuta (Element) Nakshatras are classi ed into Prithvi (Earth), Apas (Water), Agni (Fire), Vayu (Wind), Aakash (Ether).  42
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Nakshatra Orientation There are 3 types of Nakshatra Orientation. Adho Mukha (Facing Downwards) - All activities where the mind/ body is facing down or downward focused are good to start in Adho Mukha nakshatra. These includes digging wells, underground tunnels, bore wells, mining and drilling, spiritual activities since it require going deep into meditation, spiritual retreats, burying treasures or burying the dead, study of astrology, black magic, yantra and tantra can all be initiated in when Moon transits Adho Mukha nakshatras. Adho Mukha is an indication of Tamas Guna, which can be contro
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Moon transits Adho Mukha nakshatras. Adho Mukha is an indication of Tamas Guna, which can be controlled and suppressed well by planets such as Mars, Saturn, Rahu and Ketu. Urdhwa Mukha (Facing Upwards) - All activities requiring the mind/ body be facing up or upward focused are sure to succeed in the Urdhwa Mukha nakshatra. Launching of space missions and missiles, joining a new job, institution, clubs causing the reputation to go up or get rise in career, making new investment can all be initiated in when Moon transits Urdhwa Mukha nakshatras. Urdhwa Mukha is an indication of Sattwic Guna, w
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: ated in when Moon transits Urdhwa Mukha nakshatras. Urdhwa Mukha is an indication of Sattwic Guna, which can be controlled and harnessed well by planets such as Sun, Moon and Jupiter.  43
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Tiryanga Mukha (Facing Forward/Straight) All activities that require the mind/ body to be facing straight or looking forward wherein continuity is required can sure meet success in Tiryanga Mukha nakshatra. Sowing seeds, visiting or receiving friends, buying vehicles, cars, manufacturing, etc. can all be initiated in when Moon.  44
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Animal Symbol and Gender (Yoni) The animal symbol associated with each nakshatra can provide a lot of information about the characteristics of the nakshatra. It has a lot of esoteric signi cance. Traditionally the animal symbol/yoni is used to determine sexual compatibility in marriage between partners. But if you dig deeper you will discover a lot of similarities between the characteristics of the animal and the associated nakshatra. You can also unravel deeper meanings of these animal associations when you relate these animals to mythological stories. We will discuss this in more detail when
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: ions when you relate these animals to mythological stories. We will discuss this in more detail when we talk about each nakshatra.  45
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Bird (Pakshi) Each nakshatra is associated with a bird. In Rigveda Hamsa is a mythical bird having the ability to separate Soma from water, when these two  uids are mixed, and in later Vedic literature milk from water when these two are mixed. Also Hamsa is the vehicle of the Ashwins in Rigved and in later Vedic literature of Brahma. Apart from the normal meaning of aquatic birds like goose, gander, swan,  amingo, hamsa also carries the meaning soul or spirit (typi ed by the pure white color of a goose or swan and migratory like a goose; sometimes the universal soul or supreme spirit, identi e
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: a goose or swan and migratory like a goose; sometimes the universal soul or supreme spirit, identi ed with Narayana, Vishnu, Shiva, Kama and the Surya). The commentator of Rigveda Sayana takes the symbol of Hamsa to be derived from "Aham Sah" which means "I He", which signi es that the individual soul is one with the universal spirit "I am Brahman." Compare the famous Upanishadic expression "Jivo brahmaiva na parah"; the individual soul is Brahman and nothing else. Apart from Peacock, Mayura also carries the meanings: instrument for measuring time, a kind of gait, plant (Achyranthes aspera). B
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: o carries the meanings: instrument for measuring time, a kind of gait, plant (Achyranthes aspera). Baka is a kind of heron or crane. It also can mean a cheat, rogue, because the crane is regarded as a bird of great cunning and deceit in certain circumstances.  46
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Direction Each nakshatra is associated with a direction. Nakshatra Lochana/ Drishti This can be particularly helpful in  nding lost items based on the nakshatra that was operating when it was lost. Andha Lochan - Revati, Rohini, Pushya, Uttraphalguni, Vishakha, Purvashada, Dhanishta.  47
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Manda Lochan- Ashwini, Mrigashira, Ashlesha, Hasta, Anuradha, Uttara Ashada, Shatbhisha. Madhya Lochan- Bharani, Adra, Magha, Chitra, Jyeshtha, Abhijeet, Purvabhadrapad. Sulochan - Krittika, Punarvasu, Purva Phalguni, Swati, Mula, Shravana, Uttrabhadrapad. 1. If the item was stolen in Andha Lochan, then it can be recovered quickly from the east direction. 2. If the item was lost in Manda Lochan, then it can be recovered from the south direction within 3-4 days with a lot of much trouble. 3. If the item was lost in Madhya Lochan, then it is in the west direction. The information on that item is
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: he item was lost in Madhya Lochan, then it is in the west direction. The information on that item is obtained after a month from the day it was lost. Sometimes it may also take around 2.5 months. 4. If the item is lost in Sulochan Nakshatra, then it is in the North direction. But you may never get any information about the item and may not be able to  nd it.  48
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Sounds (Nakshatra Nama) Each nakshatra and its pada has a sound associated with it. And this is particularly used to name a child. In India a child is named according to the nama of the nakshatra pada of the natal moon.  49
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Tree Each Nakshatra is associated with a tree. A practical remedy for nakshatras is to nurture the tree that represents the nakshatra of your natal moon.  50
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: Vargottama, Pushkara Navamsa and Pushkara Bhaga Vargottama Planets can bring strength and steadiness and give solid success For Example #1: Venus in Chitra Nakshatra 2nd Pada is in its debilitated Sign of Virgo. This would make the karakatwa of Venus weak being in the debilitated Navamsa. So, this may indicate there could be issues in marriage or may indicate the partner can be crafty and cunning with interest in arts, photography, music, interior designers, architecture, interior designs, gemology, clothing and jewelry making. There could be passive aggression in the native s spouse being in
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

chunks.text: ogy, clothing and jewelry making. There could be passive aggression in the native s spouse being in a Mars nakshatra. However, the debilitated in uence of Venus will have tempered and the native will overcome the negativity and Venus. Planets in Pushakara Navamsa are highly auspicious and act as though they are exalted.  55
chunks.source: Research on 27 Nakshatras (Arjun Pai) (Z-Library)

There are no Pushkara Navamsas in Mercury Nakshatras (Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, and Revati) and Mars Nakshatras (Mrigashira, Chitra and Dhanishtha) and Ketu Nakshatras (Ashwini, Magha and Mula) 2. The 2nd Pada of Moon Nakshatras (Rohini, Hasta, Shravana), Saturn Nakshatras (Pushya, Anuradha and Uttara Bhadrapada) and Jupiter Nak

chunks.text: Sapta Shalaka Chakra (Vedha of Nakshatras) The purpose or use of Sapta Shalaka Chakra is to identify Nakshatra Vedha and timing of good and bad periods based on transit of focal planets. This can also be used to predict transit results of planets traversing di erent Nakshatras vis- -vis Janma Nakshatra. The interpretation of the Sapta Shalaka Chakra is simple and it is read as follows: Nakshatra opposite to each other causes Nakshatra Veda. For example, Bharani causes Veda to Magha and vice versa.  58

chunks.text: Nakshatras and Animal Totems Every species of animal is unique and gifted in its own way to be able to survive in di erent habitats and thrive. Our seers studied the traits, abilities and observed common animalistic instincts in human beings. They associated each of the nakshatras to fellow animal totems. We can categorise the nakshatras broadly into 3 groups of 9 consecutive nakshatras as: Ashwini to Ashlesha (Rajasic), Magha to Jyeshtha (Tamasic) and Moola to Revati (Sattvic). The Story of Chyavana Rishi In Hindu mythology, Sukanya was the daughter of Sharyati, son of Vaivasvata Manu and the wife of the great sage Chyavana. The sage had spent so long in meditation that he was covered by a crow s nest. The beautiful girl Sukanya came upon the nest and saw two shining objects inside. Not realizing these were the eyes of the sage, she poked playfully at them, and the sage was blinded. Chyavana was enraged, and Sukanya s father placated him by o ering her in marriage. After their marriage Sukanya served the sage cheerfully,

One day she was spotted by the Ashwini Kumaras, identical twins who served as physicians of the gods, who decided that her ethereal beauty was worthy of residence in heaven rather than languishing on the Earth serving an old blind sage. They asked her to marry one of them. Being a faithful wife, she vehemently objected to their request. chunks.text: CHAPTER 1 INTRODUCING MUNDANE ASTROLOGY Astrology is a complex field with many different branches. Mundane astrology, which makes predictions about the political and economic condition of nations, is one of those branches. Despite the obvious importance of its subject matter who doesn t want to know in advance about the political and economic future of the nation they live in? it has been relatively neglected over the last century or so. Recently, however, astrologers in many countries have begun to revive the classic techniques of mundane astrology and put them to use. Like every branch of th
chunks.source: The Astrology of Nations Casting and Interpreting Charts For Nations, Politics,

chunks.text: n to revive the classic techniques of mundane astrology and put them to use. Like every branch of the ancient science of the stars, mundane astrology requires a firm grasp of the basics of astrological science. This first chapter will attempt to provide that. If you already know your way around natal astrology the most popular branch of astrology, the one that deals with individual birth charts you will find some things about mundane astrology very familiar and others very strange. If you don t know a thing about astrology yet, don t worry this book will provide you with everything you need to

chunks.text: Let s begin with a few definitions, so everyone is clear on what is being discussed. Astrology is the empirical science and craft of the correlations between planetary movements and human affairs. Its earliest surviving records date from more than five thousand years ago in valleys of the Tigris and the Euphrates Rivers, in what is now Iraq. The scholars of several ancient cultures in that area hypothesized that there might be connections between events here on Earth and the observed movements of the Sun, Moon, and planets, and they started keeping records in an effort to find out what those c
chunks.source: The Astrology of Nations Casting and Interpreting Charts For Nations, Politics,

chunks.text: f the Sun, Moon, and planets, and they started keeping records in an effort to find out what those connections might be. That was, as scientists nowadays like to say, a fruitful hypothesis. By 1600 BCE, astrologers were making detailed predictions based on the patterns their forebears had observed. By 600 BCE, horoscopes in the modern sense of the word had come into use. Greek, Roman, Arabic, and Persian scholars in the centuries that followed made their own contributions to astrology. So did the astrologers of medieval and Renaissance Europe, and of course the same thing is true of every corn
chunks.source: The Astrology of Nations Casting and Interpreting Charts For Nations, Politics,

chunks.text: e astrologers of medieval and Renaissance Europe, and of course the same thing is true of every corner of the modern world as well. Astrology today remains an active, evolving field full of ongoing research and lively disputes. Mundane astrology is the oldest branch of astrology, the one that analyzes and predicts political and economic trends on the basis of planetary movements. The kind of astrology that most people think of first, the astrology of individual personality and destiny as shown in birth charts, is called natal astrology or, if you prefer a more old-fashioned term, genethliac as
chunks.source: The Astrology of Nations Casting and Interpreting Charts For Nations, Politics,

chunks.text: n birth charts, is called natal astrology or, if you prefer a more old-fashioned term, genethliac astrology. There are several other branches of astrology: horary or divinatory astrology, which answers specific questions; electional astrology, which determines the most auspicious time to begin an action or new project; medical astrology, which assists in the diagnosis and treatment of illnesses; and others. While they share a basic theoretical structure and many other features in common, each branch of astrology has its own tools and techniques, which have evolved over the centuries as astrolo
chunks.source: The Astrology of Nations Casting and Interpreting Charts For Nations, Politics,

chunks.text: anch of astrology has its own tools and techniques, which have evolved over the centuries as astrologers checked their charts and predictions against events. Keep this in mind, because one common mistake of the inexperienced is trying to use the techniques of natal astrology in mundane work. Mundane charts are cast in the same way as natal charts, but their delineation that is, the analysis of factors and their synthesis into a complete picture follows different rules.

chunks.text: The planets are the main active indicators in astrology. The word  planets  in ancient Greek literally means  wanderers,  and in earlier times it stood for every visible object that moves noticeably against the background of the stars. Later on, scientists divided things up further. Astrologers who want to be precise these days speak of the Sun and Moon as  luminaries,  and Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune as  planets.  (The dwarf planets Ceres, Pluto, and Eris, along with an assortment of smaller bodies, belong in a different category; we ll get to them a little late
chunks.source: The Astrology of Nations Casting and Interpreting Charts For Nations, Politics,

chunks.text: ith an assortment of smaller bodies, belong in a different category; we ll get to them a little later.) Each planet has a distinctive influence on human affairs, and the condition and relationships of each planet in relation to the whole chart can be used to predict how things will turn out here on Earth. No, nobody knows why. In astrology we re in the position of people who lived before the time of modern physics, who knew that rocks fall when you drop them, but couldn t tell you why that happens. This is why I described astrology as an empirical science. We don t know the mechanism by which
chunks.source: The Astrology of Nations Casting and Interpreting Charts For Nations, Politics,

We don t know the mechanism by which astrological effects work, and given the prejudices of modern science, it s unlikely that we ll get funding for the necessary studies any time soon. The fact that the cause is unknown, however, doesn t keep the effect from being real. Did rocks fall any differently before Isaac Newton figured out the laws of gravity? Mercury is variable he can be benefic or malefic depending on context while the Sun is generally benefic but acts like a malefic when in conjunction with other planets. A planet conjunct the Sun is termed combust, and that means just what it looks like: the energies of the planet are burned up by the Sun, metaphorically speaking, and have very little effect. The elements are easy to understand if you treat them as metaphors, and tradition assigns qualities to each element to help with this: fire is hot and dry; earth, cold and dry; air, hot and moist; and water, cold and moist. The modalities are also easy to understand because they have to do with qualities of action: the influence of cardinal signs tends to come on strong and fade out quickly, that of fixed signs is stable and difficult to budge, and that of mutable signs is elusive,

(In ancient times, the constellations used to be in the signs, which is where the confusion comes from.) The signs are regions of space counted from the point in the heavens where the Sun is located at the moment of the spring equinox. That s 0  , which is pronounced  zero degrees Aries. Dignity and debility are the astrological terms for the strength or weakness of planets. A planet that is dignified has a stronger or more positive influence than usual, and the aspects of human affairs that it represents will share in that strength or positivity. A planet that is debilitated has a weaker or more negative influence than usual, and the aspects of human affairs that it represents will share in that weakness or negativity.
chunks.source: The Astrology of Nations Casting and Interpreting Charts For Nations, Politics,

chunks.text: There are two kinds of dignity and debility. Essential dignity or debility comes from the planet s placement in the zodiac, while accidental dignity or debility comes from the planet s placement in the houses, and from the aspects between planets (we ll get to houses and aspects shortly).
